stem: For a frequency distribution with 120 observations, the less-than ogive and the more-than ogive intersect at the point (47, 60). What is the median of the distribution?

per_option_rationale.rationale: The x-coordinate of the intersection of the less-than and more-than ogives gives the median. The intersection at (47, 60) means the median is 47.
Using the y-coordinate (60) of the intersection point instead of the x-coordinate. The y-value at intersection equals N/2, not the median.
Reading the total number of observations (120) as the median, confusing N with the median value.
Halving the y-coordinate (60/2 = 30) or the x-coordinate (47/2 = 23.5), confusing the computation of N/2 with the median itself.

explanation: The less-than ogive rises from 0 to N, and the more-than ogive falls from N to 0. They intersect when CF = N/2 = 60. The x-coordinate at this intersection is the median. Given the intersection at (47, 60), the median is 47.

explanation_sections.punchline: Median = x-coordinate of the intersection of the two ogives = 47.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the model: reading the median from ogive intersection. The less-than ogive has cumulative frequency = N/2 at the median. The more-than ogive also has cumulative frequency = N/2 at the median. Their intersection is at (median, N/2). Intersection point is (47, 60) and N = 120, so N/2 = 60 confirms the y-value. Therefore median = 47.
explanation_sections.lesson: The x-coordinate of the intersection of the two ogives gives the median. The y-coordinate at the intersection always equals N/2.
explanation_sections.timing: 15 seconds. The x-coordinate of the intersection is the median. Trap: option 2 (60) is the N/2 value, not the median.
